.qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r7/task/solution/app/server.js (versions table, TIMER_OPTIONS; feasibility of fix only)
evidence: Built a requirement->criterion map across instruction.md and the three /instructions notes against all 2 gate + 16 functional + 6 polish + 4 visual criteria. Nearly every requirement maps (walls on every route incl. live wall, client scope, signed-out data, replies 3 deep with quotes and cross-matter refusal, edits/versions/stale edit, delete confirm, author-only delete, held-undeletable, placeholders, formatting everywhere incl. earlier versions, message links/previews/highlight, mentions incl. case/suggestions/edit-in/out/delete, unread per user/tab/new-line/mark-unread, Enter/Shift+Enter/Escape, idempotent send, same-time ordering, live updates preserving draft/scroll/open reply, 390px (transcript_print + phone_chambers), timer boundary/shorten/off/lengthen/partner-only, hold scope/release, literal case-insensitive search, transcript contents, refusal-in-place, symlink refusal in test.sh). Runtime items (port, NODE_PATH, DB_PATH, health, non-/app cwd, ordinary user) are shared template policy enforced by test.sh, not task gaps. Ungraded asked-for behaviors found: (1) integration.md line 5 says restarts keep 'edits and their versions', but persistence step c (scored/functional/judge.toml line 276) only checks JUDGE-S0 'shows edited' -- no criterion re-reads an earlier version after restart_app, the only restart in the suite. (2) walls-and-retention.md line 23 offers timers 'off, 1 day, 7 days or 30 days'; timer_changes (lines 139-142) only exercises 7, off and 30, so the 1-day option is never graded. (3) Minor/partial: integration.md says new edits carry the fixed clock time; no criterion inspects an edit's or earlier version's timestamp. Not counted as gaps: client access to earlier versions (brief says staff can, not that clients cannot), general refusal-in-place beyond sign-in (mapped to refusal_in_place; breadth is row 31). Static review only; no judge or Docker run was performed for this row.
counterexample: App that persists messages/edited flag/holds/walls/timers in SQLite but keeps earlier-version history in an in-memory Map (or rebuilds the versions table on startup): after restart_app the 'Versions' viewer is empty, yet every persistence step-c item reads identically and all other criteria (which never restart) pass. Separately, an app whose timer control offers only off/7/30 days passes timer_changes and every other criterion despite the stated 1-day option.
suggested_fix: In persistence step c, add as a noted item: 'as Harriet open JUDGE-S0's earlier versions: "Persist parent JUDGE-S0" is listed', re-checked in leg 1 after restart. In timer_changes, add a check that the timer control offers off, 1 day, 7 days and 30 days (or set M-13 to 1 day in an intermediate leg before off, with a positive control), keeping the existing 7/off/30 legs. Optionally note in the edits criterion that a version or edit time shown reads 2026-05-12 11:00. Re-run workload/judge evidence after the change.
